issues.description: Template placeholder 'url = ""  # CI fills this' remains in committed code. Code style rule 5 explicitly lists this pattern as a forbidden template placeholder that should be filled in by the adapter. The url attribute should point to the recipe hosting repository or be removed.
issues.fix_suggestion: Set url to the recipe repository URL (e.g., the cnb.cool制品仓 recipe path) or remove the '# CI fills this' comment and set an appropriate value.

issues.description: patch_description values do not follow the required '序号 描述' format (e.g., '0001 Add cmake...'). All 8 patch_description entries start with a free-form description instead of the 4-digit patch number prefix. Code style rule 12 specifies: patch_description should use space-separated format starting with the patch number, e.g. "0001 build aux config.guess".
issues.fix_suggestion: Prefix each patch_description with the corresponding 4-digit patch number, e.g. change "Add cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.5) for CMake 4.x compatibility" to "0001 Add cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.5) for CMake 4.x compatibility".

issues.description: test.c matches the R34 empty-shell-test pattern: it only prints 'cdrkit test_package structure check: OK' and returns 0 without calling any cdrkit API. This exactly matches the R34 deception example 'int main() { printf("test passed\n"); return 0; }'. While the overall test_package is NOT deceptive because conanfile.py test() method executes real binaries (genisoimage --version, isoinfo --version, ISO creation and reading), the test.c file itself is a placeholder. For a tool package (application, not library) there is no C API to call, so this is understandable, but the file should document this more clearly or ideally perform a minimal structural check (e.g., verify a header exists).
issues.fix_suggestion: Either (a) add a comment at the top of main() explicitly stating 'This file is a build structure placeholder; real tests run in conanfile.py test() via self.run()', or (b) if cdrkit ships any public headers, include one and perform a minimal compile-time check.

issues.description: The CMakeLists.txt defines a fake CTest test: add_test(NAME cdrkit_binary_test COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E echo "cdrkit test placeholder"). This test always passes without testing anything. While conanfile.py test() runs real binary tests via self.run() before calling cmake.test(), the CMake-level test itself is a no-op placeholder. This is borderline R9 (fake pass) — the cmake.test() call will report success for this placeholder test.
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove the add_test() placeholder line, or replace it with a real test command that invokes a cdrkit binary with --version and checks the exit code.

issues.description: Unused import: 'import os' is present but 'os' module is never referenced anywhere in the main conanfile.py. All path manipulation is done via Conan APIs (self.dependencies, CMakeToolchain).
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove the 'import os' line from the main conanfile.py.

issues.description: Unused import: 'import shutil' is present but shutil module is never used in the test_package conanfile.py. All file operations use os.path, os.makedirs, and open().
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove the 'import shutil' line from test_package/conanfile.py.

issues.description: test_package only verifies genisoimage and isoinfo binaries (ISO creation and reading). It does not test wodim (CD/DVD writer), which is the primary tool in cdrkit and involves hardware access (capget/capset, SCSI). While testing actual CD/DVD writing requires physical hardware, a 'wodim --version' or 'wodim -help' smoke test could verify the binary at least loads and links correctly, especially given the extensive wodim patches (0007, 0008) involving kernel capget/capset API adaptation.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a 'wodim --version' or 'wodim checkdrive -version' smoke test in conanfile.py test() to verify the wodim binary runs and links correctly on the target platform.

summary: Audit of cdrkit 1.1.11 Conan recipe (feat/cdrkit-1.1.11 branch, 18 changed files). VERDICT: PASS. No P0 (deception) or P1 (recipe correctness) issues found. The recipe demonstrates genuine OHOS platform adaptation: 8 well-crafted patches address real platform gaps (pthread_cancel→graceful shutdown, libcap→kernel capget/capset, __THROW fallback, rcmd/setreuid/setregid disablement, CMake 4.x compat, extern outfile for lld). Source URL (ftp.debian.org) is official and HTTPS. sha256 is valid (64 hex chars, not zero/fake). manifest status 'published' is consistent with notes.md. commands.json correctly declares cdrkit as a tool. test_package conanfile.py runs real binary tests (genisoimage/isoinfo version checks + ISO create/read roundtrip). 4 P2 warnings: (1) template placeholder url='' in conanfile.py, (2) patch_description format non-compliant, (3) test.c is an R34-pattern empty shell (compensated by conanfile.py real tests), (4) CMakeLists.txt add_test is a no-op placeholder. 3 P3 hints: unused imports (os in main conanfile, shutil in test_package), and missing wodim smoke test. No forbidden files, no pre-compiled binaries, no CI gate bypass, no status file leakage.
